strengths: **Well-motivated problem with concrete evidence (Section 3.1, Figure 2).** The paper identifies a real and previously overlooked mismatch, backed by specific data: HASS's gains concentrate on 1st-ranked tokens while degrading or stagnating on lower-ranked tokens that constitute ~45% of tree nodes. This empirical grounding is stronger than a purely conceptual motivation.

**Clean, principled solution (TALF, Algorithm 1).** The tree-aware loss is a natural fix: train the draft model on the same tree structure it will use at inference. The approach of using the target model to pre-generate tree structures and aggregating per-node cross-entropy losses is conceptually simple and directly aligns training with the inference objective.

**Thorough ablation isolating both contributions (Table 2).** Testing all 9 combinations of (beam search / optimal tree search / SALF) × (EAGLE-2 loss / HASS loss / TALF loss) cleanly separates the benefits of the new loss function from those of the new tree construction method. TALF improves mean generation length (τ) consistently across all three tree construction methods (7–13% over EAGLE-2, 4–7% over HASS). This level of disentanglement is rare and valuable in SpD papers.

**Consistent speedups across diverse settings.** Improvements hold across 3 target models (Llama2-7B, Llama3-8B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B), 5 tasks, and 2 temperatures. The pattern of larger gains for stronger target models (DeepSeek) is internally coherent with the paper's thesis.
**No architecture change required.** The method works within the existing EAGLE draft model architecture, making integration into serving frameworks (vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, SGLang) straightforward.
weaknesses: **Unequal training budgets partially confound the headline EAGLE-2 comparisons.** For Llama2-7B and Llama3-8B, EAGLE-2 is evaluated after 10 training epochs, while HASS and TALF receive 10+3=13 epochs (lines 196–198). The 15.6–39.4% improvement claims over EAGLE-2 are therefore partially confounded — part of the gain may come from longer training rather than from TALF's tree-aware objective. **However**, this does not invalidate the paper: (a) the HASS comparisons (6.5–24.4%) are clean since both methods receive 13 epochs and already show meaningful improvements; (b) the DeepSeek setup uses equal wall-clock time (24 hours); (c) Table 2's ablation shows TALF consistently outperforms regardless of tree construction method. The authors should retrain EAGLE-2 for matched epochs to cleanly resolve this.

**TALF drops the regression loss (used by both EAGLE and HASS for feature alignment) without an ablation study.** Line 114 states it was "sufficient" without empirical support. An ablation comparing TALF with and without ℒ_reg would clarify whether this design choice is optimal or if the regression loss could further improve performance.

**No confidence intervals or variance reported.** With 5 benchmarks per condition and single-run evaluations, it is difficult to assess whether the reported differences between methods are statistically significant. While this is common practice in the SpD literature, the paper would be strengthened by reporting variance across runs or bootstrapped intervals.

**No explicit verification that the output distribution matches the target model's distribution.** The paper claims "without any generation quality degradation" but tree-based verification can deviate from exact guarantees depending on the acceptance scheme. A brief empirical check (e.g., perplexity on a held-out set, or output agreement rate with the target model) would substantiate this claim.

**Preprocessing cost for TALF training not quantified.** Having the target model generate trees over 68k dialogues (line 110) has a non-trivial computational cost. Reporting this overhead would help practitioners evaluate adoption.
